title: Development of a Patient Satisfaction Measure for Primary Care Behavioral Health (PCBH) Settings: A Delphi Study.
abstract: Studies of patient satisfaction with Primary Care Behavioral Health (PCBH) services are limited, and those that exist have either used general satisfaction measures not specific to integrated care or researcher-developed, unvalidated measures. Development of a psychometrically validated measure of patient satisfaction that captures unique elements of this model would support clinical quality improvement efforts and enable more rigorous evaluation of the PCBH model. This study gathered expert feedback using Delphi methodology to inform the development of a measure of patient satisfaction specifically for PCBH settings. Purposive sampling was used to identify experts (n = 20). Participants rated possible measure items on a scale of (1) "Very Irrelevant" to (5) "Very Relevant" as an indicator of patient satisfaction with PCBH and provided open-ended feedback on item wording across two Delphi rounds. The resulting measure of patient satisfaction includes 20 items that capture key aspects of both visit satisfaction and PCBH model satisfaction. Next steps include assessing the psychometric properties of this measure in a sample of PCBH patients. Through the development, validation, and dissemination of this measure, we hope to add to the PCBH patient outcome literature, an area that is currently lacking in our field.

journal.name: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL PSYCHOLOGY IN MEDICAL SETTINGS
